answer: My answer to sybils is Community-detection penalty for dense clusters — a cluster of accounts that only talk to each other — which makes the harbor of cheating a bill the attacker pays again for every clone. Because a cluster of accounts that only talk to each other, a fresh identity starts with nothing: it must earn its standing the slow way, while the anchor for an established agent is already paid and proven. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The horizon grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
